I've read the complete file. The diff is small and purely UI-facing: it introduces an `"already"` status branch, threads the server's `result.status` into local state, and swaps the copy shown to the user. No new sinks, no new data sources, no new authorization boundaries. The rendered text is static strings (React auto-escapes anyway), and `result.status` is compared with `===` against a literal — even if attacker-controlled it can only pick between the two rendered strings.

The only meaningful security concern in this diff is the user-enumeration disclosure ("You're already on the list."), which the prior reviewer already flagged. I do not see a distinct second vulnerability in the +lines here.
